title: Copper price sinks into bear market, erasing 2026 gains in worst week of the year
zh_title: 铜价陷入熊市，抹去2026年涨幅，为今年最糟糕的一周
summary: 铜价周五再次暴跌，在创下历史新高仅十周后，铜价就进入熊市，因为对人工智能热潮的押注解除、强势美元和美国关税前景的黯淡继续掩盖了中国严重短缺的证据。纽约最活跃合约 Comex 12 月交割铜价一度下跌 3.4%，至每磅 5.4405 美元（每吨 11,994 美元），为 3 月底以来的最低水平，午盘左右回升至 5.4995 美元，跌幅 2.4%。这比 9 月 9 日达成的创纪录的 6.8885 美元结算价低 20.2%。收盘价低于 5 美元。
content:
铜价周五再次暴跌，在创下历史新高仅十周后，铜价就进入熊市，因为对人工智能热潮的押注解除、强势美元和美国关税前景的黯淡继续掩盖了中国严重短缺的证据。纽约最活跃合约 Comex 12 月交割铜价一度下跌 3.4%，至每磅 5.4405 美元（每吨 11,994 美元），为 3 月底以来的最低水平，午盘左右回升至 5.4995 美元，跌幅 2.4%。这比 9 月 9 日创下的 6.8885 美元的创纪录结算价低 20.2%。收盘价低于 5.51 美元将符合熊市的常见定义，即较最近的峰值下跌 20% 或更多。该合约已连续七个交易日下跌，自上周五以来已下跌超过 9%，为 2026 年迄今为止最大单周跌幅。9 月份迄今为止的涨幅为 22%，目前已下跌 2%，而铜价到 11 月底预计将下跌约 15%。据路透社报道，伦敦金属交易所三个月期铜在官方交易中下跌 2.3%，至每吨 12,235 美元，此前触及 12,020 美元，为 3 月 24 日以来的最低水平。该基准指数本周下跌约 9%，这是自 2025 年 4 月初美国总统唐纳德·特朗普公布全球关税以来的最大单周跌幅。伦敦铜价比 9 月 10 日峰值 14,875 美元低 18%，并且必须跌破 11,900 美元才能与纽约市一样进入熊市。
据彭博社报道，在上海，期货创下 15 年来最糟糕的一周表现。下一站，3 月份的低点，跌破 5.63 美元（2025 年铜价结束时的价格），消除了盛宝银行 (Saxo Bank) 的 Ole Hansen 在周三暴跌期间标记的两个图表支撑中的第一个。第二个价格为 5.32 美元，略低于 2026 年的最低收盘价：3 月 20 日的 5.34 美元，当时伊朗战争期间油价飙升和交易所库存膨胀导致金属跌至三个月低点。目前铜价比该水平高出不到 3%。 Capital.com 高级金融市场分析师凯尔·罗达 (Kyle Rodda) 向路透社表示，越来越多的证据表明，人工智能投资热潮正在减弱，美联储将不得不更加积极地控制通胀，并补充说，美元走强也给黄金带来压力。该通讯社称，周五 AI 股价继续下跌，Anthropic 上市后股价较周四收盘价下跌约 9%。 Benchmark Mineral Intelligence 的铜分析师 Albert Mackenzie 告诉彭博社：“只要人工智能一直在推动价格上涨，我们就一直在说，这可能有点过分了。”中国需求疲软、美国关税和美元前景黯淡也在发挥作用，本周的损失与大流行初期和特朗普宣布解放日之后的暴跌相差不远。伦敦铜正面临 2022 年以来最大幅度的月度跌幅。
金属流向中国 期货抛售仍在继续，同时中国对实物金属的争夺仍在继续。 据路透社报道，周五，进口铜到中国所支付的洋山溢价从周四创纪录的每吨 500 美元下滑至 495 美元。周三价格为 360 美元，9 月份还不到 100 美元。上海期货交易所库存本周增加 3,204 吨至 30,846 吨，仍低于中国一天的消费量。这种紧张可能是导致期货下跌的部分原因。这些水平的溢价使得将金属运出美国变得有利可图，过去一年美国库存激增

【原文 English Original】
Copper slumped again on Friday, tipping the metal into a bear market just ten weeks after it set an all-time high, as the unwinding of bets on the artificial intelligence boom, a strong dollar and fading US tariff prospects continued to swamp evidence of acute shortage in China. Comex copper for December delivery, the most active contract in New York, dropped as much as 3.4% to $5.4405 a pound ($11,994 a tonne), the lowest since the end of March, before recovering to $5.4995 around midday, down 2.4%. That is 20.2% below the record settlement of $6.8885 reached on September 9. A close under $5.51 would meet the common definition of a bear market, a fall of 20% or more from the most recent peak. The contract has fallen for seven sessions in a row and is down more than 9% since last Friday, by far its steepest weekly loss of 2026. A year-to-date gain that stood at 22% in September has turned into a loss of 2%, and copper is on course to end November about 15% lower. On the London Metal Exchange, three-month copper fell 2.3% to $12,235 a tonne in official trading after touching $12,020, the lowest since March 24, Reuters reports. The benchmark is down about 9% on the week, its biggest weekly fall since early April 2025, when US President Donald Trump unveiled his global tariffs. London copper is 18% below its September 10 peak of $14,875 and would have to drop under $11,900 to join New York in a bear market. In Shanghai, futures racked up their worst week in 15 years, according to Bloomberg. Next stop, the March low The break below $5.63, where copper ended 2025, removes the first of two chart supports that Saxo Bank’s Ole Hansen flagged during Wednesday’s rout . The second is $5.32, which sits just beneath the lowest close of 2026: $5.34 on March 20, when surging oil prices during the Iran war and swelling exchange inventories sent the metal to a three-month trough. Copper is now less than 3% above that level. Evidence is mounting that the AI investment boom is waning and that the Federal Reserve will have to get more aggressive to control inflation, Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, told Reuters, adding that a strengthening dollar is also weighing on the metal. AI shares continued to sag on Friday, with Anthropic trading about 9% below Thursday’s close after its market debut, the news agency said. “We have been saying for as long as AI has been driving the price that this might be a bit over-egged,” Albert Mackenzie, copper analyst at Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, told Bloomberg. Weak Chinese demand, the dimming prospect of US tariffs and the dollar are also at work, and the week’s losses are not far off the slumps seen in the early stages of the pandemic and after Trump’s Liberation Day announcement. London copper is heading for its steepest monthly decline since 2022 . Metal heads to China The selloff in futures is still running alongside a scramble for physical metal in China. The Yangshan premium paid to import copper into the country slipped to $495 a tonne on Friday from Thursday’s record $500, Reuters reports. It was $360 on Wednesday and less than $100 in September. Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks rose by 3,204 tonnes this week to 30,846 tonnes, which is still less than a day’s worth of Chinese consumption. That tightness may be part of what is pushing futures down. Premiums at these levels have made it profitable to move metal out of the United States, where stockpiles ballooned over the past year on tariff bets, and traders have begun shipping copper from the US to China , with tens of thousands of tonnes due to arrive in January. Codelco is meanwhile offering Chinese buyers 2027 cathode at $250 to $280 a tonne , less than it charged this year. The flow looks set to continue. China’s refined copper imports are poised to climb in 2027 after a rare drop this year, according to a Reuters poll of 15 analysts and traders, because shortages of concentrate and scrap are holding back domestic smelter output while demand keeps growing. Imports fell 16% to 2.37 million tonnes in the first ten months of 2026, the lowest for the period since at least 2015. “The gravitational pull of refined copper is now towards China,” said Nicholas Snowdon, head of metals and mining research at Mercuria, although Argus expects a moderate recovery rather than a surge. In London the squeeze has eased: cash copper was at only a slight premium to the three-month contract on Friday after flipping into a discount earlier in the week. $127 billion in a week Copper stocks were sold again in New York. Eleven of the largest copper-exposed miners have lost a combined $127 billion, or 15% of their market value, since last Friday, and $208 billion, or 23%, over the past month. Their combined worth has dropped to $696 billion from $769 billion on Wednesday morning. Freeport-McMoRan fell another 5.4%, taking its loss for the week to 22% and cutting its market value to $67 billion, from close to $100 billion a month ago. Southern Copper gave up 4.3% to $116 billion and has shed 32% in a month, a slide that has pushed the stock into the red for 2026 after it was up 41% in mid-October. BHP was little changed at $177 billion but is down 14% on the week, and Rio Tinto eased 1.3% to $127 billion. Glencore, at $71 billion, has lost a fifth of its value in a month. Teck Resources dropped 3.6% to $24 billion, Antofagasta 4.8% and First Quantum Minerals 3.7%, and Lundin Mining’s 2.3% decline left it 19% lower since last Friday. Only BHP, Glencore, Teck and Anglo American are still showing gains for the year, and Anglo’s is down to 1%. Ivanhoe Mines has lost 60% in 2026. (With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

title: Ground View Pakistan: The smelter before the mine
zh_title: 巴基斯坦地面景观：矿井前的冶炼厂
summary: 在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。 “在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区
content:
在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。谢里夫说：“在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区。”这一举措反映出巴基斯坦希望从矿产财富中获取更多就业机会、技能和出口收入。但由于只有山达克 (Saindak) 一家铜矿生产厂，其旗舰 Reko Diq 项目仍在等待商业生产，该国面临着更紧迫的挑战：在投入数十亿美元建设加工基础设施之前建立可靠的矿山产出。巴基斯坦联邦规划、发展和特别倡议部长阿赫桑·伊克巴尔表示，政府现在要求投资者提交完整的价值链提案，而不是仅仅关注开采和原材料出口的计划。这一要求给探险家带来了特殊的挑战。铜冶炼厂是围绕特定精矿设计的，包括其品位、杂质和预期产量。
如果没有明确的矿产资源和可靠的生产，开发商就无法做出贷款人要求的原料承诺。Milbank 律师事务所能源和基础设施合伙人穆尼布·侯赛因 (Munib Hussain) 表示，合同原料是此类项目融资的主要要求之一。区别很重要。 2025 年 4 月，我认为仅靠采矿并不能实现关键的矿产独立性，因此应优先考虑对加工的投资。这一论点涉及美国，美国现有的矿藏和数十年的生产为下游投资奠定了基础。巴基斯坦正处于早期阶段，全球铜市场呈现出不同的经济现实。冶炼经济 随着中国的新设施与印度、中亚和非洲不断扩大的业务展开竞争，铜冶炼厂正面临产能过剩的困境。处理和精炼费用方面的压力显而易见，矿工向冶炼厂支付费用，将精矿转化为精炼金属。安托法加斯塔和中国冶炼厂同意 2026 年基准为每吨 0 美元和每磅 0 美分，低于 2025 年每吨 21.25 美元和前一年的 80 美元。现货费用已降至零以下，标准普尔全球普氏能源资讯 (S&P Global Platts) 1 月份的评估值为每吨负 47.40 美元。这些负费用意味着加工商实际上正在向矿工支付费用以确保精矿。
Wood Mackenzie 副总裁兼金属和采矿咨询主管帕特里克·巴恩斯 (Patrick Barnes) 在论坛上表示：“现在是建设冶炼厂的非常艰难的时期。”印度说明了其中的商业风险。阿达尼 (Adani) 价值 12 亿美元的卡奇铜冶炼厂每年需要约 160 万吨精矿才能满负荷运营。彭博社报道的进口记录显示，该公司在 2024 年 2 月至 2026 年 2 月期间获得了所需原料的四分之一以上。有关高杂质精矿相关运营不稳定的报道加剧了人们的担忧，尽管阿达尼对这些说法提出了异议。在其他地方，嘉能可关闭了位于菲尔州的帕萨尔冶炼厂

【原文 English Original】
Pakistan’s ambition to build a domestic copper processing industry risks putting smelters ahead of mines at a time when global refining capacity already exceeds available concentrate supplies.  Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reinforced that ambition at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad, pledging to end exports of unprocessed minerals and calling for Reko Diq and other projects in the southwest to support refineries, smelters and factories producing cables and conductors.  “Mine in Pakistan, process in Pakistan, manufacture in Pakistan and then export to the rest of the world,” Sharif said.  The push reflects a desire to capture more jobs, skills and export revenue from Pakistan’s mineral wealth. But with only one producing copper operation, at Saindak, and its flagship Reko Diq project still awaiting commercial production, the country faces a more immediate challenge: establishing reliable mine output before committing billions to processing infrastructure.  Ahsan Iqbal, Pakistan’s federal minister of planning, development and special initiatives, said the government now asks investors to submit complete value-chain proposals rather than plans focused solely on extraction and raw-material exports.  That requirement creates a particular challenge for explorers. Copper smelters are designed around specific concentrates, including their grades, impurities and expected volumes. Without defined mineral resources and dependable production, developers cannot establish the feedstock commitments lenders require.  Munib Hussain, an energy and infrastructure partner at law firm Milbank, said contracted feedstock ranks among the principal requirements for financing such projects.  The distinction is important. In April 2025, I argued that mining alone would not deliver critical minerals independence and that investment in processing should take priority.  That argument concerned the United States, where established mineral deposits and decades of production provided a foundation for downstream investment. Pakistan is at an earlier stage, and the global copper market presents a different economic reality.  Smelting economics  Copper smelters are struggling with excess capacity as new facilities in China compete with expanding operations in India, Central Asia and Africa.  The pressure is evident in treatment and refining charges, which miners pay smelters to convert concentrate into refined metal.  Antofagasta and Chinese smelters agreed to a 2026 benchmark of $0 per tonne and zero cents per pound, down from $21.25 per tonne in 2025 and $80 the previous year. Spot charges have fallen below zero, with S&P Global Platts assessing them at minus $47.40 per tonne in January.  Those negative charges mean processors are effectively paying miners to secure concentrate.  “It’s a very tough time to build a smelter,” Patrick Barnes, vice-president and head of metals and mining consulting at Wood Mackenzie, said at the forum.  India illustrates the commercial risks. Adani’s $1.2-billion Kutch Copper smelter requires approximately 1.6 million tonnes of concentrate annually to operate at full capacity. Import records reported by Bloomberg indicate it secured just over a quarter of its required feedstock between February 2024 and February 2026.  Reports of operating instability linked to high-impurity concentrate have added to concerns, although Adani has disputed those accounts.  Elsewhere, Glencore has closed its Pasar smelter in the Philippines, while Australia has intervened to support the Mount Isa smelter in Queensland.  Even countries that have developed mines before building processing facilities remain exposed to supply disruptions.  Indonesia delayed its copper concentrate export restrictions until production at Grasberg, one of the world’s largest copper mines, could adequately supply domestic smelters. Freeport also had to demonstrate that sufficient concentrate had been reserved for its Manyar facility.  But a September 2025 mud rush at Grasberg forced Freeport to declare force majeure, leaving Indonesian processors short of material.  For Pakistan, these examples strengthen the commercial case for Reko Diq’s existing development plan.  The project is designed to export copper concentrate by rail to Port Qasim for shipment through the Pakistan International Bulk Terminal. Although that approach falls short of the government’s downstream ambitions, it positions Pakistan to benefit from the current shortage of concentrate rather than compete in an oversupplied smelting market.  Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said Reko Diq’s first year of commercial production had been expected to generate $2.8 billion in exports, equivalent to roughly 10% of Pakistan’s current goods exports.  For an economy repeatedly constrained by balance-of-payments crises, that potential foreign exchange revenue is significant.  The opportunity also extends to Western supply chains. American and allied processors need dependable mineral supplies, making Pakistan’s emerging mining industry potentially more valuable as a concentrate exporter than as another entrant into copper smelting.  Domestic processing could still make economic sense for smaller, specialized operations targeting minerals with genuine refining bottlenecks and committed buyers. Antimony is one example, with at least one Pakistani processor pursuing refining capacity linked to prospective US offtake.  Exploration incentives  Pakistan’s taxation policies present another obstacle to establishing the mining industry needed to support future processing.  Waleed Ahmed Vohra, founder and chief executive of Pakistani explorer Ark Metals, said customs duties and taxes consume close to 30% of his exploration budget because the emerging industry depends heavily on imported equipment and foreign technical services.  “I really feel bad when I have to raise a hundred dollars and give 30 dollars to the government,” Vohra said.  Rather than seeking permanent exemptions, he proposes deferring those obligations until commercial production begins, allowing companies to invest more capital in exploration while preserving the government’s eventual tax revenue.  “Defer now to prosper tomorrow,” he said.  Aurangzeb acknowledged the industry’s concerns and said the government would consider changes to taxation and other policies, particularly measures supporting exporters. He pointed to the removal of super taxes in this year’s budget.  But he also emphasized Pakistan’s limited fiscal flexibility, warning that a tax-to-GDP ratio below 10% would be unsustainable. The country has only recently moved into double digits.  That creates a policy dilemma. Export-oriented tax relief provides little immediate benefit to explorers that may spend years defining deposits before generating revenue.  Deferral could bridge that gap without permanently eliminating government receipts, although it would postpone collections and leave the treasury exposed if projects never reach production.  Current incentives nevertheless favour processing.  At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif announced the province’s first dedicated mineral processing zone at an industrial estate in Khushab, offering industrial land at nominal rent for 15 years alongside customs duty concessions.  Federal relief for explorers, including a reported 30-year sales tax exemption covering exploration and development, remains under consideration.  The contrast is striking: processing investors are receiving concrete incentives while explorers are still seeking comparable support.  Government officials appear increasingly aware of the sequencing challenge. Barnes said discussions at the forum showed that policymakers had carefully examined the conditions necessary to make domestic smelting commercially viable.  “They understand that until there’s a mining industry here, smelting is not really on the table,” he said. “If they get two, three, four mines that are producing, options start to open up for them.”  Pakistan does not need to abandon its processing ambitions. It needs to distinguish between commodities where domestic refining addresses a genuine supply-chain shortage and copper, where existing smelters are already competing for scarce material.  The immediate priority is to make exploration more attractive, establish dependable production and build an export industry capable of financing future downstream investment.  A domestic copper smelter may eventually make sense. Its economic justification will be stronger once Pakistan has several producing mines and the concentrate supply to sustain it.  For now, the furnace can wait for the rock.  * Erik Groves is a contributing analyst for MINING.COM and Corporate Strategy and In-House Counsel at Morgan Companies. He will attend and provide coverage of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad on November 12 and 13. Event organizers are assisting with travel, accommodation, and interview coordination with key participants. Neither Groves nor MINING.COM is receiving payment for coverage. All reporting, analysis, interview selection and editorial decisions remain independent of the organizers, who have no right to review or approve content before publication .

title: Trump, Xi agreed that military AI decisions should involve humans, Bessent says
zh_title: 贝森特表示，特朗普和习近平一致认为，军事人工智能决策应让人类参与
summary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。 “我认为特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与 SI 做出的任何军事决策，SI 应该
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。贝森特表示：“我认为，特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与情报情报机构做出的任何军事决策，并且不应允许情报情报机构在重大军事行动中自主行事，这一点非常重要。”贝森特指的是特朗普政府对该技术的首选术语“超级智能”。贝森特表示，美中就该技术的军事使用达成的协议需要人类参与和其他保障措施，不会受到两国人工智能霸主竞争的影响。他补充说，美国人工智能实验室需要保持其技术领先地位，作为抵御网络攻击中使用的“危险”中国人工智能模型的最佳防御手段。贝森特说：“但是，当双方都同意不应该在无人参与的情况下发起任何重大军事行动时，这与竞争无关。”
他表示，涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名与他有恋情的中国公民的间谍指控并未在特习双边会晤中提及。贝森特表示，在特朗普采取他所谓的“非常强硬的路线”后，英伟达的第二级人工智能芯片 H200 仍然是中国可以通过许可购买的最先进的芯片。 “我认为我们看到的是中国人在 H200 上的订单很少，因为他们试图构建自己的芯片堆栈，而且我认为他们可能落后了很多年，”他补充道。英伟达丑闻发生后，贝森特淡化了财政部长和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在人工智能芯片限制问题上所表达的分歧，称特朗普政府官员“都致力于遵循特朗普总统的指示”。美国商务部周一采取措施，进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，包括中国实体可以租用计算能力的海外数据中心使用的芯片。 “我认为我们将会看到适当的芯片限制已经到位，并且远程访问已经被限制，”他说。

【原文 English Original】
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday. Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump’s trip to Asia. “I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology, “super intelligence.” Bessent said that the U.S.-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries’ competition for AI supremacy. He added that U.S. AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against “dangerous” Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks. “But there’s nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved,” Bessent said. He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting. Bessent said that Nvidia’s second-tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a “very firm line.” “I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind,” he added. Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were “all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.” The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power. “I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed,” he said.

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，尤其是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
zh_title: 中国攻击者部署人工智能代理，自主发现并利用 0day 来接管大学服务器
summary: 亚马逊首席信息安全官 CJ Moses 表示，可疑的中国间谍部署了人工智能代理，这些代理可以自主工作，在开源应用程序中查找零日漏洞，然后利用该缺陷闯入大学网络，从而完全控制服务器。与中国有关的攻击者使用了 Cairn，这是一个开源渗透测试框架，该框架越来越受到网络犯罪分子的欢迎，他们使用人工智能工具在没有人工协助的情况下进行多阶段入侵。在本例中，特工发现并利用了零日 MONAI Label，这是一种开源医学成像 AI 应用程序。亚马逊通知
content:
亚马逊首席信息安全官 CJ Moses 表示，可疑的中国间谍部署了人工智能代理，这些代理可以自主工作，在开源应用程序中查找零日漏洞，然后利用该缺陷闯入大学网络，从而完全控制服务器。与中国有关的攻击者使用了 Cairn，这是一个开源渗透测试框架，该框架越来越受到网络犯罪分子的欢迎，他们使用人工智能工具在没有人工协助的情况下进行多阶段入侵。在本例中，特工发现并利用了零日 MONAI Label，这是一种开源医学成像 AI 应用程序。亚马逊将该漏洞通知了该项目的维护人员，他们发布了修复程序和安全公告。 Moses 在周五与 The Register 分享的一份报告中表示，9 月 10 日，亚马逊的威胁情报团队发现了一个带有公开托管的 Cairn 实例的服务器，该实例可以让人们了解针对中国大陆以外东亚地区大学的活动。该活动从 9 月 8 日开始持续了 48 小时，提示是用简体中文编写的，执行脚本中的时间戳配置为中国标准时间。
然而，在人工智能代理发现并利用零日漏洞之前，他们试图在大约 16 小时内进行 148 次连续操作，闯入另一所大学的 Redis 服务器，包括滥用 Redis 的复制功能来加载未经授权的代码、逃离其脚本沙箱、写入其配置文件以及损坏其内存。这些都没有成功，当这些操作失败时，代理还尝试针对不同的服务进行 Log4Shell 注入，即服务器端请求伪造 (SSRF) 攻击针对共置 Qdrant 实例中的漏洞，以及针对 PostgreSQL、SSH 和其他工具的多个凭据喷射。与此同时，一项持续了 6 个多小时的单独行动针对一所大学 GPU 服务器进行了另一次凭据喷雾攻击，编制了在学校公共网站、学术论文和其他文件中发现的 80 个真实用户名的列表。摩西写道：“这两次行动都没有成功，但它们一起表明，特工们在没有人类指导的情况下持续适应了近一整天。”随后，AI 代理发现了 MONAI Label 中的零日路径遍历漏洞，这次他们能够访问服务器。摩西写道：“代理识别了应用程序的框架，映射了其 API 端点，并找到了带有文件名参数的上传端点。”他们测试了该参数的路径遍历，发现该参数存在漏洞。
在大约 11 分钟内，代理从映射应用程序的 API 转变为在服务器上任意写入文件。”随后，代理滥用相同的缺陷来执行以 root 身份运行的 Python 反向 shell。在另一个会话中，代理发现零日漏洞后，人类操作员向他们提供了一个代理，该代理通过隧道进入第二个大学网络，并连接到运行相同易受攻击代码的服务器。亚马逊的发现是在 Gambit Security 威胁情报团队的早期报告之后进行的，该报告还记录了一名中国操作员使用 Cairn除了 Cairn 之外，攻击者还使用另外两个开源 AI 工具窃取了一家财富 500 强酒店公司、一家美国大型航空公司和一家大型私营企业的信用卡记录和其他敏感数据，并“在不同程度上”对至少 27 家公司进行了攻击。

【原文 English Original】
Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents which worked autonomously to find a zero-day in an open source application and then abuse the flaw to break into university networks, gaining full control of a server, according to Amazon CISO CJ Moses. The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance . In this case, the agents found and exploited a zero-day MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon notified the project's maintainers of the vulnerability, and they released a fix and a security advisory . On September 10, Amazon's Threat Intelligence Team found a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn that provided visibility into the campaign targeting universities in East Asia, outside Mainland China, Moses said in a Friday report shared with The Register . The campaign occurred over a period of 48 hours beginning on September 8, and the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese, with timestamps in executed scripts configured to China Standard Time. Before the AI agents found and exploited the zero day, however, they tried to break into another university’s Redis server over about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions, including abusing Redis's replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory. None of these were successful, and when those actions failed, the agents also attempted a Log4Shell injection against a different service, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack against a vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance, and several credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and other tools. Meanwhile, a separate operation running for more than 6 hours targeted a university GPU server with another credential-spray attack, compiling a list of 80 real user names found across the school’s public websites, academic papers and other documents. "Neither operation succeeded, yet together they show that the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction," Moses wrote. Then the AI agents found the zero-day path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label, and this time they were able to gain access to the server. "The agents identified the application's framework, mapped its API endpoints, and found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter," Moses wrote. They tested that parameter for path traversal, and the parameter was vulnerable. In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application’s API to arbitrarily writing files on the server." Later, the agents abused the same flaw to execute a Python reverse shell running as root. In another session, after the agents discovered the zero-day, the human operator provided them with a proxy that tunneled into a second university network, and connected to a server running the same vulnerable code. Amazon's discovery follows an earlier report by Gambit Security's threat intelligence team that also documented a Chinese operator using Cairn to carry out at least 105 attacks, and managing to compromise, "to varying degrees," at least 27 companies. This campaign also occurred in September. In addition to Cairn, the attacker used two other open source AI harnesses to steal credit card records and other sensitive data from a Fortune 500 hospitality company, a major US airline, a large private US industrial supplies distributor, and a US online fashion retailer, and other companies. "Together, these cases show that this autonomous AI agent framework is being adopted in both espionage and criminal operations," Moses wrote. ®

title: The Hydrogen Stream: China starts operating 195 km hydrogen pipeline
zh_title: 氢气流：中国开始运营195公里氢气管道
summary: 据新华社报道，中国已开始运营连接达尔汗木明干联合旗和内蒙古包头市的一条全长195公里的氢气管道。该管道的批准年运输能力为10万吨氢气，有可能增加到24万吨。该基础设施由内蒙古华电华盟管道开发，将连接包头北部的可再生氢气生产设施与南部的工业消费者。据了解，管道运输可以将氢气运输成本从管式拖车的约 13 元/公斤（1.83 美元）/公斤降低到约 3 元/公斤。
content:
据新华社报道，中国已开始运营连接达尔汗木明干联合旗和内蒙古包头市的一条全长195公里的氢气管道。该管道的批准年运输能力为10万吨氢气，有可能增加到24万吨。该基础设施由内蒙古华电华盟管道开发，将连接包头北部的可再生氢气生产设施与南部的工业消费者。据新华社报道，管道运输可以将氢气输送成本从管式拖车的约 13 元/公斤（1.83 美元）/公斤降低到约 3 元/公斤。中国一直在扩大氢能运输基础设施，以将可再生能源与工业需求连接起来。 ACME集团已就印度奥里萨邦投资36亿美元的绿色氨项目达成最终投资决定（FID），该项目年产能76万吨。该设施计划于 2029 年投入运行，将配备由蒂森克虏伯伍德设计的日产 2,200 吨的氨生产回路。它将利用可再生电力通过电解生产氢气，用于绿色氨生产，目标客户是印度、日本和欧洲。 Brookfield 已承诺提供高达 6 亿美元的资金来支持 ACME 的绿色分子平台。该项目预计每年可避免超过150万吨温室气体排放。 ACME还在印度获得了绿色氨供应合同，并正在开发绿色甲醇项目。
智利的研究人员发现，通过减少太阳能发电生产的绿色氢气可以实现低至 5.58 美元/公斤的氢气平准化成本 (LCOH)，而最具竞争力的风电项目为 7.27 美元/公斤。这项名为“减少太阳能发电的绿色氢气：真实数据分析”的研究评估了 2023 年 7 月至 2024 年 6 月期间 56 个太阳能发电厂和 44 个风电场的运营数据，总装机容量为 10.4 吉瓦。大约 25% 的记录每小时间隔发生这种情况，主要是在低功率水平下发生。研究人员利用基于质子交换膜 (PEM) 电解槽的技术经济模型，确定了 10 个表现最佳的项目（全部位于智利北部）的最佳电解槽容量为可再生发电厂净有效功率的 5% 至 13%。这些项目实现了 LCOH 值 5.58 美元/公斤至 6.97 美元/公斤，电解槽容量系数为 25% 至 30%。与最佳电解槽尺寸偏差高达 50% 的氢气生产成本增加不超过 3.8%。这项即将发表在《能源报告》上的研究发现，尽管储存、压缩和运输成本仍然是额外的考虑因素，但减少可再生电力可以支持具有竞争力的氢气生产。智利经历了严重的可再生能源削减，特别是在该国北部的太阳能发电厂。 Qair 在法国奥克西塔尼开设了 Hyd’Occ 可再生氢气生产设施。

【原文 English Original】
China has started operating a 195 km hydrogen pipeline connecting Darhan Muminggan United Banner with Baotou, Inner Mongolia, reported Xinhua News Agency. The pipeline has an approved annual transport capacity of 100,000 tons of hydrogen, potentially increasing to 240,000 tons. Developed by Inner Mongolia Huadian Huameng Pipeline, the infrastructure will connect renewable hydrogen production facilities in northern Baotou with industrial consumers in the south. Pipeline transport could reduce hydrogen delivery costs from about CNY 13 ($1.83)/kg by tube trailer to approximately CNY 3/kg, according to Xinhua. China has been expanding its hydrogen transport infrastructure to connect renewable energy resources with industrial demand. ACME Group has reached a final investment decision (FID) on a $3.6 billion green ammonia project in Odisha, India, with an annual production capacity of 760,000 tons. The facility, scheduled for commissioning in 2029, will feature a 2,200-ton-per-day ammonia production loop designed by Thyssenkrupp Uhde. It will use renewable electricity to produce hydrogen through electrolysis for green ammonia production, targeting customers in India, Japan and Europe. Brookfield has committed up to $600 million to support ACME’s green molecules platform. The project is expected to avoid more than 1.5 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually. ACME has also secured green ammonia supply contracts in India and is developing green methanol projects. Researchers in Chile have found that green hydrogen produced from curtailed solar electricity could achieve a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) as low as $5.58/kg, compared with $7.27/kg for the most competitive wind projects. The study, “ Green hydrogen from curtailment: Real data analysis ,” assessed operational data from 56 solar plants and 44 wind farms with a combined capacity of 10.4 GW between July 2023 and June 2024. Curtailment occurred in about 25% of recorded hourly intervals, predominantly at low power levels. Using a techno-economic model based on proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers, the researchers identified optimal electrolyzer capacities of 5% to 13% of the renewable plants’ net effective power across the 10 best-performing projects, all located in northern Chile. The projects achieved LCOH values of $5.58/kg to $6.97/kg, with electrolyzer capacity factors of 25% to 30%. Deviations of up to 50% from optimal electrolyzer sizing increased hydrogen production costs by no more than 3.8%. The study, to be published in Energy Reports , found that curtailed renewable electricity could support competitive hydrogen production, although storage, compression and transport costs remain additional considerations. Chile has experienced significant renewable energy curtailment , particularly at solar plants in the north of the country. Qair has inaugurated its Hyd’Occ renewable hydrogen production facility in Occitanie, France. The 20 MW plant is supported by a regional network of hydrogen refueling stations forming part of the European H2 Corridor. Qair opened its first hydrogen refueling stations in Béziers and Narbonne in spring 2026. A second development phase will double the plant’s installed capacity to 40 MW, increasing annual hydrogen production capacity to 5,400 tons. Total investment amounts to €130 million. Plug Power has launched GenEco Scale, an integrated electrolyzer plant offering for utility-scale hydrogen production. Arcadia eFuels has selected the system for a 280 MW hydrogen facility at its Project ARC development in Texas. Plug Power said it has completed the project’s technical evaluation and front-end engineering design (FEED) study. Once operational, the facility is expected to support production of approximately 23.2 million gallons of electro-sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) annually. Plug Power previously signed a 280 MW electrolyzer supply agreement with Arcadia eFuels for a separate project in Denmark. Protium has completed due diligence for two green hydrogen projects under the UK government’s second Hydrogen Allocation Round (HAR2). The South Tees Net Zero project in northern England and the South Wales Net Zero project have both advanced to the Invitation to Offer stage. The 70 MW South Tees facility is designed to produce up to 11,000 tons of green hydrogen annually, equivalent to about 433 GWh, for industrial consumers in Teesside. The projects will now progress toward Low Carbon Hydrogen Agreements, which provide revenue support to reduce investment risks. Protium is also developing other UK hydrogen projects , including a 15 MW electrolyzer project that secured support under the first Hydrogen Allocation Round. title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
zh_title: 美国情报报告发现俄罗斯正在研发太空核武器
summary: 上个月，美国国防情报局（DIA）发布了一份令人毛骨悚然且信息丰富的报告，评估了美国对手在太空中构成的威胁的范围和广度。新报告重点关注中国、俄罗斯以及伊朗和朝鲜等新兴太空强国。它着眼于地球轨道及更远的地方正在发生的事情，包括地月空间，即我们的星球和月球之间的区域。该报告是 2026 年版的《太空安全挑战》，是国防情报局针对美国国家安全面临的太空相关挑战和威胁进行的第三次非机密情报评估。
content:
上个月，美国国防情报局（DIA）发布了一份令人毛骨悚然且信息丰富的报告，评估了美国对手在太空中构成的威胁的范围和广度。新报告重点关注中国、俄罗斯以及伊朗和朝鲜等新兴太空强国。它着眼于地球轨道及更远的地方正在发生的事情，包括地月空间，即我们的星球和月球之间的区域。这份报告——2026 年版的《太空安全挑战》——是国防情报局对美国国家安全面临的太空相关挑战和威胁以及太空在国际上被视为作战领域的程度进行的第三次非机密情报评估。您可以在此处阅读报告中的信息，截至 2026 年 7 月为最新信息。DIA 的使命是提供有关外国军队的情报，以帮助预防战争并赢得战争。该报告的初步发现是，中国、俄罗斯、伊朗和朝鲜正在“以威胁所有太空系统安全及其相关太空利益的方式”开发、测试、部署和使用太空能力。事实上，中国和俄罗斯正在发展“一系列强大的”进攻能力，以削弱或摧毁其他国家的太空服务，从动能破坏到复杂的干扰和网络行动。
DIA 报告还指出，“生产更便宜、更小、更简单的卫星，开发和部署速度更快，加上商业发射服务的扩展，正在推动商业太空替代方案的快速整合，以支持国家安全。”国防情报局的报告补充说，虽然太空商业化正在使以前以政府为中心的太空服务广泛地提供给感兴趣的各方，但这种可用性还包括具有恶意利益的国家和非国家行为者。天基服务面临着一系列威胁，包括商业和军事服务。有些是可逆的，而另一些则是不可逆的。 （图片来源：DIA） Counterspace 担忧 DIA 处理的一个主要项目是“Counterspace”——而且它不是你在厨房里找到的那​​种。太空对抗行动可以是进攻性的，也可以是防御性的。它们可被有意用于可逆或不可逆地拒绝、扰乱、降级、损坏或摧毁空间物体或空间系统的组成部分。以下是国防情报局报告中指出的反太空关键要素： 反卫星 (ASAT) 导弹旨在对卫星进行动能打击和摧毁。反卫星导弹可能会产生大量碎片，这些碎片可以在轨道上停留数十年甚至数百年。针对地面站点和其他支持太空操作的地面基础设施的物理或网络攻击也可能威胁卫星服务。
网络反空间攻击的目标是传输信号中的卫星数据以及使用、传输和控制数据流的系统。电子攻击包括针对一个国家对电磁频谱的使用的干扰和欺骗技术。电子攻击可能会干扰用于通信以及军事部队指挥和控制的系统，包括有人驾驶和无人驾驶车辆。定向能武器（DEW）可以暂时或永久致盲图像收集卫星，并影响头顶上的持久红外和天气传感器，从而使监视、跟踪和瞄准部队的能力丧失。太空中的“繁荣时期”？时间

【原文 English Original】
Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. Physical or cyberattacks against ground sites and other terrestrial infrastructure supporting space operations can also threaten satellite services. Cyber counterspace attacks target the satellite data within the transmission signal, along with the systems that use, transmit and control the flow of data. Electronic attacks include jamming and spoofing techniques to target a nation's use of the electromagnetic spectrum. Electronic attacks can interfere with systems used for communications and command and control of military forces, including piloted and unpiloted vehicles. Directed-energy weapons (DEWs) can temporarily or permanently blind image-collecting satellites and affect overhead persistent infrared and weather sensors, thereby denying the ability to monitor, track and target forces. 'Boom time' in space? The DIA report underscores that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon . Russia is doing so despite its obligation to comply with the 1967 Outer Space Treaty . That U.N. agreement prohibits the placement of any objects carrying nuclear weapons, or any other kinds of weapons of mass destruction, into orbit around Earth. "A space-based capability such as this could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world," the DIA report states, "as well as to the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial and national security services they provide." A nuclear detonation in space could be tailored to impact satellites in most orbits, the DIA report warns, from low Earth orbit for commercial and reconnaissance satellites, geosynchronous orbit for critical communications, and medium Earth orbit for navigation and timing satellites. This graphic identifies the various destinations for spacecraft relatively close to Earth, including cislunar space. (Image credit: DIA) Cislunar developments The newly issued DIA report also observes that exploring cislunar space is of increasing interest to spacefaring nations for potential scientific and economic opportunities. However, nations such as China "may be exploring military applications from cislunar space," the report notes. China has stated its goal of developing a cislunar space economy by 2045. "China is also the first country to attempt sustained operations on the far side of the moon , with numerous projects slated to support that effort through the next decade. China portrays its interest in cislunar space as peaceful, but PRC [People's Republic of China] officials have also discussed pursuing military capabilities in cislunar space," the report states. DIA appraisals Placing a keen eye on the DIA report is Peter Garretson, a senior fellow in defense studies at the American Foreign Policy Council and a strategy consultant who focuses on space and defense. According to Garretson, the most significant positive change from earlier DIA appraisals is the explicit assessment that Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon. He told Space.com that the DIA's expanded treatment of the threat of a nuclear weapon on orbit reflects concerns in the Congress and the Trump White House. However, Garretson also flagged what he said is a consequential omission in the report: the disappearance of the prior treatment (in the 2022 version of the report) of research competition, surveillance beyond geosynchronous Earth orbit and the potential military use of deep space for staging reserve forces. Puzzle pieces In Garretson's view, the DIA needs to help put the puzzle pieces together for Congress and the attentive public about what exactly China is doing, and how it fits together in the nation's strategy to achieve comprehensive space dominance. According to Garretson, "everything they are doing, from launch cadence, reusable launch, commercial space investment, investments in power, propulsion, repair, manufacturing, to commercial assets working together" supports both an economic expansion toward new resources and what China hopes will be overwhelming military power and strategic depth. China's mysterious Shenlong space plane, imaged by a Vantor satellite in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor) Outlook for the future Garretson senses the moves by China to develop extractive and in-space industries "is truly the strategic threat that could crush American space power. Now is the time to be making the investments to ensure we have a 'freedom's forge' and 'arsenal of democracy' in space that can protect the open space commerce that is the nation's strategy." As for the DIA's outlook for the future: The agency concluded that space almost certainly will remain an increasingly competitive and crowded environment as space capabilities improve and other countries seize opportunities in the final frontier. "The increase of Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean counterspace capabilities, rapid growth in the number of space objects, and the proliferation of requirements for space-enabled services," the DIA report states, "will all complicate operations in space in the coming decade."

title: Trump defends ‘fantastic’ ties with Xi, Putin after summit backlash
zh_title: 峰会遭到强烈反对后，特朗普捍卫与习近平和普京的“出色”关系
summary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五为他与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京的“重要”峰会进行了辩护，因为他从中国回国，面临中期选举后的严厉批评和动荡。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 20 日在华盛顿特区的白宫詹姆斯·S·布雷迪新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/法新社。回国后的第二天，特朗普在白宫举行的新闻发布会上表示，他与中国和俄罗斯领导人的“良好关系”有助于确保美国的安全。特朗普部分
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五为他与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京的“重要”峰会进行了辩护，因为他从中国回国，面临中期选举后的严厉批评和动荡。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 20 日在华盛顿特区的白宫詹姆斯·S·布雷迪新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/法新社。回国后的第二天，特朗普在白宫举行的新闻发布会上表示，他与中国和俄罗斯领导人的“良好关系”有助于确保美国的安全。当他们在深圳会面时，特朗普有争议地称普京为“我的朋友”，之后特朗普特别捍卫了他与普京的关系，并坚称克里姆林宫老板真心希望结束俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。特朗普对记者说：“我们举行了多年来最重要的国际峰会之一。”他补充说，世界主要核大国领导人之间存在“巨大的电力”。 “我与普京的关系非常好。这是一件非常好的事情。我与习主席的关系非常好。
这是一件好事，我们的国家因此而安全。”不过，特朗普补充说，他不确定无核化——美国总统称无核化是中国峰会的主要议题之一——“能够实现”。这位80岁的老人在白宫讲台上的两侧是副总统万斯和国务卿马可·鲁比奥，五角大楼负责人皮特·赫格斯和财政部长斯科特·贝森特坐在附近。在美国媒体和他的民主党对手嘲笑这次峰会只不过是给跛脚鸭总统拍照的机会之后，特朗普试图宣扬这次峰会的成就，此举“令人尴尬”。在本月早些时候美国中期选举惨败后，他抵达亚洲寻求胜利，伊朗战争仍在继续，白宫面临即将上任的民主党领导的国会的多项调查。 2025 年 10 月 30 日，中国国家主席习近平在韩国釜山金海国际机场航站楼出席中美双边会议。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。但特朗普-习近平-普京的会议几乎没有产生什么具体成果，除了特朗普在新闻发布会上在画架上展示的简短的“和平宣言”，其中没有提到伊朗或乌克兰。众议院民主党党鞭凯瑟琳·克拉克 (Katherine Clark) 在 X 节目上表示：“特朗普在世界舞台上令人尴尬。”“没有什么可以结束他的伊朗战争。对乌克兰没有任何帮助。没有任何关于人工智能安全的内容。
相反，他只是痴迷于独裁者。”美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 表示，这次会议对特朗普来说只不过是“一次恰逢其时的合影”，但对习近平和普京来说，这“证明了他们的愿景，即世界正在经历根本性的权力再平衡”。毫不奇怪，特朗普在长达一小时零二十八分钟的新闻发布会上花了大部分时间来反驳对与华盛顿主要对手的独裁领导人会面的批评。他说，在与普京的双边会晤中，这位俄罗斯领导人“明确表达了他希望看到通过外交手段结束乌克兰战争的愿望”。当被问及是否认为普京是美国的朋友时，特朗普表示“我无法与美国交谈”，但补充说，他们“非常良好的关系……给了我们很多额外的力量”。与此同时，特朗普猛烈抨击“失控”的国际刑事法院，并表示普京对国际刑事法庭并不满意，该法庭已向俄罗斯发出逮捕令。

【原文 English Original】
US President Donald Trump on Friday defended his “momentous” summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin as he returned home from China to face bitter criticism and turmoil after the midterm elections. U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during a news briefing in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on November 20, 2026 in Washington, DC. Photo: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/AFP. Speaking at a news conference in the White House the day after flying back, Trump said his “fantastic relationships” with the Chinese and Russian leaders helped keep the United States secure. Trump particularly defended his ties to Putin after controversially calling him “my friend” when they met in Shenzhen — and insisted that the Kremlin boss genuinely wanted to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. “We had one of the most momentous international summits in many years,” Trump told reporters, adding that there was “great electricity” between the leaders of the world’s main nuclear powers. “I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That’s a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That’s a good thing, and our country is safe because of that.” Trump however added that he was unsure whether denuclearization — which the US president said was one of the main topics of the summit in China — “can ever happen.” The 80-year-old was flanked at the White House podium by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sat nearby. ‘Embarrassment’ Trump’s bid to tout the achievements of the summit came after US media and his Democratic opponents mocked it as little more than a photo opportunity for a lame-duck president. He arrived in Asia seeking a win after a bruising defeat in US midterm elections earlier this month, with the Iran war grinding on and the White House facing multiple investigations by the incoming Democratic-led Congress. Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a China-US bilateral meeting at the Gimhae International Airport terminal, in Busan, South Korea, on October 30, 2025. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. But the Trump-Xi-Putin powwow produced few concrete results except a brief “Declaration toward Peace” — which Trump displayed on an easel during his news conference — that made no mention of Iran or Ukraine. “Trump is an embarrassment on the world stage,” House Democratic whip Katherine Clark said on X. “Nothing to end his Iran war. Nothing to help Ukraine. Nothing about AI safety. Instead, he’s just obsessing over dictators.” Broadcaster CNN said the meeting was little more than “a well-timed photo-op” for Trump — but for Xi and Putin it was a “vindication of their vision that the world is undergoing a fundamental rebalancing of power.” It was no surprise then that Trump spent much of the one hour and 28 minute press conference pushing back at criticism for meeting the autocratic leaders of Washington’s main adversaries. He said that during a bilateral meeting with Putin, the Russian leader “clearly expressed his desire to see the war in Ukraine end by diplomatic means.” Asked if he believed Putin was a friend to America, Trump said “I can’t speak to America” but added that their “very good relationship… gives us a lot of additional strength.” ‘Out of control’ Trump meanwhile lashed out at the “out of control” International Criminal Court and said that Putin wasn’t “happy” with the tribunal, which has issued an arrest warrant for the Russian leader over the Ukraine war. Vladimir Putin. File photo: Wikicommons. On Iran, Trump accused Iran of “bullshitting for 51 years” and said Tehran’s leaders “want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me.” Trump was also full of praise for Communist Party leader Xi over the clean and futuristic streets of Shenzhen, comparing it favorably with what he said were run-down, Democratic-led cities in the United States. But the Republican president struck an unusually conciliatory tone towards the Democrats, despite them threatening him with multiple investigations when they take control of Congress next year. Trump suggested he was ready to work with Congress on healthcare, the entertainment industry and possibly on migration — though said he was also ready to veto legislation if needed.

title: Research schooner Tara sets sail from Hong Kong on 18-month mission to unlock coral resilience secrets
zh_title: 研究纵帆船 Tara 从香港起航，执行为期 18 个月的任务，解开珊瑚恢复力的秘密
summary: 本月早些时候，在香港天际线的辉光下，停泊在中环十号码头的“塔拉”号科考船呈现出令人难以置信的景象。它的圆形铝制船体能够承受极地冰的压碎压力，像拇指和食指捏着的橄榄核一样突然弹出，然后随着背包漂流，直到变暖的气温松开它冰冷的抓地力。 2026 年 11 月 4 日停泊在中环 10 号码头的科学帆船塔拉号。照片：Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP。相反，这艘两桅帆船在维多利亚港仍然温暖的海水中煎熬。 “这不太舒服，”承认
content:
本月早些时候，在香港天际线的辉光下，停泊在中环十号码头的“塔拉”号科考船呈现出令人难以置信的景象。它的圆形铝制船体能够承受极地冰的压碎压力，像拇指和食指捏着的橄榄核一样突然弹出，然后随着背包漂流，直到变暖的气温松开它冰冷的抓地力。 2026 年 11 月 4 日停泊在中环 10 号码头的科学帆船塔拉号。照片：Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP。相反，这艘两桅帆船在维多利亚港仍然温暖的海水中煎熬。 “这不是很舒服，”塔拉海洋公司的宣传官员马丁·亚历山德里尼（Martin Alessandrini）在没有窗户、木板镶板的沙龙里承认道，沙龙就位于船的嘶嘶作响的发动机顶上。塔拉号于 1989 年被命名为南极洲，在这里就像一条离开水的鱼。但11月初在香港的短暂停留在很多方面都只是一次热身。在停泊在海滨后，塔拉号起航前往被称为“海洋亚马逊”的全球海洋生物多样性热点地区。它涵盖印度尼西亚、马来西亚、巴布亚新几内亚、所罗门群岛、东帝汶和菲律宾周围的热带水域，拥有世界三分之一的珊瑚礁和约四分之三的已知珊瑚物种——与近年来经历大规模珊瑚死亡和白化事件的其他地区不同，它以某种方式经受住了气候变化和污染的风暴。
船舱内悬挂着一张描绘塔拉珊瑚探险队路线的图表。照片：Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP。尽管全球范围内的珊瑚礁不断萎缩，而且日益频繁的海洋热浪使珊瑚礁恢复的时间越来越少，但珊瑚三角区仍然保持着弹性。在过去的四十年里，世界上多达一半的珊瑚礁已经消失，但三角洲的珊瑚覆盖率在同一时期内保持稳定。塔拉的使命是找出原因，并弄清楚这些知识如何帮助其他地方的珊瑚保护和恢复工作。 18个月，26次中途停留，6个国家 在18个月的时间里，16名船员将在6个国家进行26次中途停留，总行程约5万公里。一路上，他们还将从当地合作机构招募数十名科学家，对珊瑚样本进行实验。通过将碎片暴露在不同的温度下并测试它们的耐热应激能力，研究小组希望检测出更能抵抗白化的珊瑚生物标志物。这些信息可以用来支持世界各地的珊瑚恢复项目，帮助自然资源保护主义者确定如何重建珊瑚礁以更好地抵御气候压力。法国驻香港及澳门副总领事Benjamin Hubin及agnès b.全球首席运营官 Étienne Bourgois 在 Tara 的甲板上欢迎访客。照片：Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP。
法国蔚蓝海岸大学科学主任保拉·福拉 (Paola Furla) 表示：“与之前在全球或盆地规模进行的研究不同，塔拉珊瑚关注的是唯一一个主要珊瑚礁区域，尽管气候变暖趋势强劲，硬珊瑚覆盖率仍保持相对稳定。”“这为确定复原力机制提供了一个非凡的天然实验室。”塔拉珊瑚探险的规模雄心勃勃。在接下来的一年半里，来自该地区 40 多个合作机构的 70 名科学家将加入该团队。十位驻场艺术家也将登陆

【原文 English Original】
Docked at Central Pier No. 10, under the glow of the Hong Kong skyline, the research ship Tara presented an unlikely sight earlier this month. Its round aluminium hull was built to withstand the crushing pressure of polar ice, popping up like an olive pit pinched between thumb and forefinger then drifting with the pack until the warming temperatures loosened its icy grip. The scientific schooner Tara at Central Pier No. 10 on November 4, 2026. Photo: Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP. Instead, the two-masted schooner stewed in the still-warm waters of Victoria Harbour. “It’s not very comfortable,” conceded Tara Ocean advocacy officer Martin Alessandrini in the windowless, wood-panelled saloon perched directly atop the ship’s sizzling engine. Laid down in 1989 as the Antarctica , the Tara is something of a fish out of water here. But its brief stopover in Hong Kong in early November was just a warm-up, in more ways than one. After slipping its harbourfront moorings, the Tara set sail for the global marine biodiversity hotspot known as the “Amazon of the Ocean.” Encompassing the tropical waters around Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste and the Philippines, it harbours one-third of the world’s coral reefs and about three-quarters of all known coral species – and unlike other regions that have experienced mass coral death and bleaching events in recent years, it has somehow weathered the storms of climate change and pollution. A chart depicting the Tara Coral expedition’s course hangs in the ship’s saloon cabin. Photo: Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP. Even as reefs have been shrinking worldwide, and increasingly frequent marine heatwaves have left them with less time to recover, the Coral Triangle has remained resilient. As much as half of the world’s coral reefs have been lost over the past four decades, but coral cover in the Triangle has held steady over the same period. Tara’s mission is to find out why – and figure out how that knowledge can help coral conservation and restoration efforts elsewhere. 18 months, 26 stopovers, 6 countries Over 18 months, the crew of 16 will make 26 stopovers across six countries, covering a total distance of around 50,000 kilometres. Along the way, they will also pick up dozens of scientists from local partner institutions and conduct experiments on coral samples. By exposing the fragments to different temperatures and testing their heat stress resistance, the team hopes to detect biomarkers of corals that are more resistant to bleaching. This information can then be used to bolster coral restoration projects around the world, helping conservationists determine how to rebuild reefs to better withstand climatic pressures. Benjamin Hubin, Deputy Consul General of France in Hong Kong and Macau, and agnès b. Global COO Étienne Bourgois welcome visitors on Tara’s deck. Photo: Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP. “Unlike previous studies conducted at the global or basin scale, Tara Coral focuses on the only major reef region where hard coral cover has remained relatively stable despite strong warming trends,” said Paola Furla, Scientific Director at France’s Université Côte d’Azur. “This provides an extraordinary natural laboratory for identifying the mechanisms of resilience.” The scale of the Tara Coral expedition is ambitious. Over the next year and a half, the crew will be joined by 70 scientists from over 40 partner institutions around the region. Ten artists-in-residence will also step aboard in what Alessandrini calls “a very multidisciplinary approach.” Companionway on the Tara leading below deck. Photo: Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP. They have vast swathes of ocean to cover, but they are in no hurry to do so. Experts with the Tara Ocean Foundation, backed for over 20 years by French fashion house agnès b., say the expedition’s slow pace is another factor that will make its contributions unique and valuable. Unlike earlier expeditions that have swooped in to collect samples then sailed on, Tara will stay at each of its sampling sites for a month and a half, giving the team time to experiment in the aft-deck’s “wet lab,” where target coral species will be exposed to various water temperatures. Coral at Hong Kong’s Sharp Island. Photo: GovHK. “Maybe [the coral] has been pre-selected by previous heatwaves,” Alessandrini said. The second theory explaining their resilience “is that corals in the region have a different genetic biodiversity,” he added, while “the third option [is] maybe corals in the region have been changing the algae they have inside their bodies and have thus adapted to the heat stress.” Genetic analysis will also be carried out on four target coral species to determine whether there are genes in the region that provide coral with greater resistance potential. Tara at dusk on the Central Harbourfront. Photo: Ryan Ho Kilpatrick/HKFP. “Their past exposure to thermal stress, the effect of internal waves, their genetics, their algal symbionts, their microbiome, their diversity, and the way they organise themselves: these are all avenues the expedition will explore to understand what protects the reefs,” said Serge Planes, Research Director at the French National Centre for Scientific Research. Research by the Tara Ocean Foundation has been published in prestigious scientific journals such as Nature and Science , but the group is also committed to making its findings open-source. When the expedition finally concludes, its datasets will be available online for all. As efforts to protect the ocean’s endangered coral and rebuild lost reefs and communities continue – including in Hong Kong – it is hoped that the Tara Coral expedition’s findings can shore up coral conservation and restoration work far beyond the waters of the Coral Triangle. With even rebuilt and recovering coral populations inevitably exposed to the same dangers posed by warming seas and worsening pollution, Alessandrini said, researchers can work on developing “new criteria on how to build these projects and better enhance their resilience.”

title: 外包出来的监控国家：中国数字警务是如何“拼装”起来的
summary: 编按 过去二十年，中国建成了一套庞大而精密的数字监控体系。流行的解释强调党国自上而下的主导。黄靖洋（音译）这篇基于 177 次实地访谈的论文讲了另一个故事：中央定目标、压期限，却不给钱；分税制改革后财力吃紧的地方公安，只好把技术开发外包给民营企业。由此催生出公安机关与安防企业相互交织的“安全产业复合体”。作者明确表示，这个概念并不意味着这张网络威胁党国的自主性，“放权加外包”恰恰是党国灵活达成安全目标的方式。 文章的价值在于把“监控国家”还原为具体的政治经济机制：考核压力、财
content: 编按 过去二十年，中国建成了一套庞大而精密的数字监控体系。流行的解释强调党国自上而下的主导。黄靖洋（音译）这篇基于 177 次实地访谈的论文讲了另一个故事：中央定目标、压期限，却不给钱；分税制改革后财力吃紧的地方公安，只好把技术开发外包给民营企业。由此催生出公安机关与安防企业相互交织的“安全产业复合体”。作者明确表示，这个概念并不意味着这张网络威胁党国的自主性，“放权加外包”恰恰是党国灵活达成安全目标的方式。 文章的价值在于把“监控国家”还原为具体的政治经济机制：考核压力、财政约束和企业求生，共同推动了技术扩张，维稳需求本身成了产业增长的引擎。文中还有一层意涵值得注意：法治缺位不只伤及公民。地方政府拖欠货款、随意毁约、回扣成风，企业同样深受其害。作者着墨不多、却值得读者追问的是：监控由层层外包的市场主体建造和运营时，权力的边界和问责又落在何处？ 来源 Jingyang Huang, “Delegating Digital Policing: The Evolution of China’s Security-Industrial Complex,” The China Quarterly (2026), 1–17 DOI： https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305741026103105 作者介绍：香港中文大学（深圳）公共政策学院助理教授，香港科技大学社会科学博士。 摘要 一、问题与方法 中国的安防与监控产业，在短时间内帮助党国建起了大规模监控体系，还把相关技术和设备出口到海外。常见的“国家主义”叙事把这归功于党国的强力干预，例如任正非的军人背景、国企控股海康威视。作者认为这种看法片面：华为和海康早年都历经艰难的创业期，华为曾“农村包围城市”，海康的技术骨干曾不得不自寻天使投资。 作者借用“军工复合体”的说法，提出“安全产业复合体”（security-industrial complex）。这个词指公安系统、安防承包商及其支持者在采购和外包中结成的网络。作者特别说明，用这个词并不表示他认为这张网络构成威胁党国自主性的利益集团。 研究材料是 2017 至 2022 年间在广州、深圳、东莞、香港、上海、北京、杭州、长沙、武汉进行的 177 次访谈。受访者包括企业创始人和高管、行业协会负责人、中央和地方的在职或退休干部、技术专家、学者和基层公务员。作者还参考了行业年鉴、企业年报和券商报告。 二、四十年建设脉络：从“技防”到“雪亮” 起步（1979 年起）： 改革开放后，毛时代的社会控制机制逐渐松动，公安转而向技术寻求补偿。1979 年 3 月，公安部召开全国技防会议，把“安全技术防范”定为公安工作的一部分。当时的技术主要是防盗门、锁、保险箱和报警设备。直到 1990 年代末，基层公安仍主要靠传统的人力追踪。 金盾工程与平安城市（2003–2007）： 2003 年 11 月，中央提出以科技强化公安工作。2004 年，公安部启动城市报警与监控系统试点，从 49 个申请城市中选出 22 个。2005 年底起推行“3111 工程”，在每个省选一个市、每个市选一个县、每个县选一个社区作为试点。北京借奥运建设“四网”防控体系，并试行把社区划分为网格的管理方式，这就是后来全国推行的“网格化管理”的雏形。 平安建设与平安中国（2007–2014）： 第二批 38 个试点城市接受评估。监控项目在招标中常被称为“天网工程”，覆盖金融机构、学校、医院、能源设施直至住宅小区。2010 年，公安部要求 2013 年底前基本建成城市报警与监控系统。2011 年，公安部提出到 2015 年，东部、中部、西部农村地区的视频监控覆盖率分别达到 80%、70%、60%。一位退休的公安部官员用“大安防”概括这种扩张：“人、财、物、建筑，所有要保护的对象都纳入安全应用的范围。”（编译，非原话）习近平 2013 年就平安中国建设作出指示，2014 年提出“总体安全观”，安全的范围从治安扩展到“综合社会治理”。 智慧城市与雪亮工程（2015–2019）： 2015 年，国务院要求加强重点行业和城乡基层的“防控网”。同年，公安部等十部门联合发文，推动公共安全视频监控全覆盖、全联网。2016 年，中央选定 45 个城市给予视频图像专网建设补贴。2017 年，“雪亮工程”推广到街道和村一级：在路口和人群聚集处安装高清摄像头，把画面接入县、乡、村三级平台，甚至通过电视网络传到居民家中。 三、为什么外包：财政与考核的夹缝 作者认为，问题的关键在于中央与地方的分工。中央（主要是公安部）负责定目标、做考核；省、市两级掌握激励资源的分配；基层负责落实。分税制改革后，中央没有为地方早期的平安城市建设提供足够资金，任务又总是有时限的。结果是，地方公安机关越来越依赖技术外包，安防产业从公安内部的技术部门中分离出来。作者把这种现象称为地方层面的“适应性监控资本主义”。作者特别指出，强制力机关与企业界（尤其是民营企业）借助大规模政府采购结成公私联盟，要到 2009 年才真正出现。 据作者引用的研究，全国各级地方公安机关签下了全部监控相关合同的 65.8%（Batke 和 Ohlberg，2020）。 四、企业从哪里来：红色工程师、技术掮客与民营老板 体制内起步： 公安部第一研究所（北京）和第三研究所（上海）在 1984 年改组。1991 年，经公安部游说，“公安产品产业”被列为机电行业的子类，交由公安部管理，公安部由此首次获得管理这类产品和市场的职权。1980 年代，政府曾明令禁止并打击民间企业生产安防产品。转业到公安系统的军队技术人员的作用有限：据一位官员说，最好的人才都留在了军队或进了公安部。 向西方“引进来”： 广东因毗邻香港，率先通过考察和贸易引进西方的报警技术。一批有政治背景的“技术掮客”帮沿海公安引进成熟的境外产品；在六四之后西方实施技术制裁的时期，他们尤其活跃。 民营创业： 一位马来西亚出生的侨商马先生，最初靠出租安检设备起家，按报纸和电视上的演出信息逐一给安保单位打电话推销。一位 1998 年离开公安系统的创业者，凭体制内背景赢得了大量地方合同。加入世贸组织后，又一批中小企业进场，早期主要是组装境外产品。外资也起过重要作用：美国 C&K 公司从 1990 年北京亚运会起成为早期城市报警系统的主要供应商，到 1993 年全国新建的报警中心几乎都用它的产品；霍尼韦尔提供视频监控系统，华为与 3Com 的合资企业则带来了网络技术。 四万亿的转折： 受访者普遍认为，2008–2009 年的四万亿刺激计划是产业的分水岭。一位创业者说，2008 年以前，一家公司能拿到“数千万”的合同就很了不起，此后很多合同动辄“数亿”。（编译，原文货币单位写作美元） 两种建设模式： 一种是公安自建、自营、自管；另一种是由国有电信运营商出资建设运营，公安租用。2008 年以前多数地方采用后一种。以浙江为例，2008 年奥运前全省建成 45,613 个摄像头，其中公安安装 20,190 个，花费约 8 亿元，占总支出的 64%；电信运营商安装 25,423 个，花费约 4.5 亿元，占 36%。 广东的规模： 2012 至 2014 年，广东新建视频图像采集点 1,084,000 个；2015 至 2016 年又新建 765,000 个。 五、四种交易：从“承包”到长期分包 作者指出，在缺乏稳定、可信承诺的制度环境下，政企之间、企业之间的交易并不总能得到执行或法律保护。他据此归纳出四类交易： 非常规形态之一：机会主义合作。 中小企业借外国合作方急于扩张市场的机会学习技术。在知识产权保护薄弱的环境下，一些企业“借用”外方的设计起家。珠三角还形成了“山寨”产业集群，基层公安有时在不知情的情况下，就采购了这类山寨安防产品。 非常规形态之二：临时“承包”。 作者借用黄宗智区分“承包”与“契约”的思路：“承包”是上级单方面压任务，“契约”是双方对等履约。在权力不受约束、法治不完善的情况下，企业常常要承受政府的单方面要求。2001 至 2006 年间，项目高度碎片化，中小企业靠招标或人情关系在区县一级拿单，门槛低，但回款没有保障。有企业被要求在资金未落实的情况下提前完工，欠款拖了三年甚至更久，有的公司因此倒闭。2000 年代，基层项目普遍存在给官员回扣的“潜规则”，还曝光过量身定制招标条件的腐败案。这种模式对政府和市场两败俱伤。一位基层民警抱怨，某个派单系统非但没有提高效率，反而增加了一线的负担，坏了之后也找不到人维护。 常规形态之一：战略耦合。 加入世贸组织后，企业接入全球芯片、传感器和镜头供应链，通过购买专利、招聘海归和跨国公司工程师来提升研发能力，逐渐从代工（OEM）走向自主创新。少数技术巨头因此与省、市公安建立了稳定的合作关系。 常规形态之二：长期分包。 作者用“资产专用性”来解释：系统一旦建成，政府就离不开原厂的技术人员驻场维护和升级，这种依赖反过来制约了政府的任意行为。双方由此走向长期分包。但依赖也有另一面：企业可以说服政府采购并非必需的技术。一位前产品经理坦言，各个工程团队都想把自己的技术塞进系统以求生存，“其中有些技术可能并不合适”。（编译，非原话） 作者总结，这些交易形态整体上从非常规走向常规化。尽管政府违约屡见不鲜，企业仍依靠 2008 至 2016 年项目规模的急剧扩张维持利润。据受访者说，这种格局至少延续到新冠疫情结束。 六、结论与开放问题 作者认为，地方安全机构在考核压力和财政、时间约束下，放弃了内部研发，转向外包，催生了“适应性监控资本主义”（adaptive surveillance capitalism）——指地方政府在财政与考核压力下，把监控建设外包给企业，由此“自下而上”催生出一个依附于政府采购的安防产业（编者注）。安全在这里不仅是控制工具，也是推动创新的力量；党国借助灵活授权保住了自主性，同时也被它释放出的企业逻辑悄悄重塑。作者借用洪源远（Yuen Yuen Ang）的“受控的即兴”（controlled improvisation）概括这一模式，并提出两个开放问题： 国际制裁加码时，这种全球供应链耦合是否会被打断？ 安全开支不断膨胀、基层财政持续紧张，政府违约可能加剧，从而动摇支撑这个产业的激励结构。

title: 习近平治下延迟退休改革的政治

content: 编按 提高退休年龄，是各国政府都想回避的“得罪人”的改革，法国在 2023 年、俄罗斯在 2018 年都因此爆发大规模抗议。中国几乎不可能出现有组织的抗议，这项改革却从 2013 年三中全会提出，到 2024 年人大立法，整整拖了十多年。为什么？ 纽约新学院政治学教授弗雷泽（Mark W. Frazier）梳理政策文件和官方宣传后指出，中共的做法与民主国家的政客如出一辙。第一，分十年小步推进，把代价转给离退休还远、也不太关注此事的中青年。第二，先改革公职人员养老“双轨制”，平息“不公”的怨气。第三，用人大立法而非部委规章把改革定下来。作者称之为“事前”的威权回应性：中央是这项政策唯一的制定者，无法把责任推给地方，只能未雨绸缪。 这套审慎的另一面同样值得留意：草案在会议开幕前两天才提交，没有公开征求意见；改革后官员的养老金仍约为企业职工的两倍，而城乡居民养老保险的领取者每月只有两百多元。没有选票和街头抗议的约束，所谓“回应”只体现在推进节奏上，没有落实到分配公平上。 来源 Mark W. Frazier, “The Politics of Retirement Age Reform Under Xi Jinping,” The China Quarterly (2026), 1–16 DOI： https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305741026103208 作者介绍：纽约新学院社会研究学院政治学教授，新学院印中研究所联合所长 Manifestation_retraites_11_février_2023_Besançon_Toufik-de-Planoise.jpg 摘要 一、问题：一项“难中之难”的改革 2024 年 9 月 13 日，全国人大常委会通过《关于实施渐进式延迟法定退休年龄的决定》。按照这项决定，到 2035 年，女性蓝领的退休年龄从 50 岁逐步提高到 55 岁，女性白领（干部岗位）从 55 岁提高到 58 岁，男性从 60 岁提高到 63 岁。原有的退休年龄定于 1950 年代，而 2023 年中国人均预期寿命已达女性 81 岁、男性 75 岁。经济学家胡鞍钢称这项改革是“难中之难”。 前全国社保基金负责人戴相龙 2013 年曾对《中国青年报》说，退休年龄是“国家对公民的承诺”，延迟退休“可能违背与下一代的契约”。2024 年决定出台后，这篇访谈从网上消失了。决定公布当天，微博话题“逐步延迟至男63女55或58周岁退休”在 9 小时内阅读量达 10.4 亿、评论 38.6 万条，但没有任何实际抗议的报道。 作者对照俄罗斯 2018 年的经验：普京第四次当选后不久提出延迟退休，百余座城市爆发抗议，连亲克里姆林宫的工会也参与其中。普京被迫亲自上电视，把女性退休年龄的目标从 63 岁降到 60 岁。中共很可能判断自己不会遇到这样的局面，但它采取的策略，除了禁止有组织的抗议之外，与民主国家颇为相似。 财政压力是改革的直接动因。中国社科院的郑秉文 2019 年的精算报告显示，若不改革，城镇职工养老保险的累计结余最早将在 2035 年耗尽。领取该项养老金的人数从 1997 年的 2,530 万增至 2024 年的 1.474 亿，2019 年以来每年新增退休者约 600 万。总支出从 2012 年的 1.60 万亿元增至 2024 年的 6.76 万亿元。 二、改革内容：用时间换空间，把成本转给年轻人 谁受影响： 改革覆盖两大制度的 3.79 亿人，即城镇职工基本养老保险（简称“城职保”），以及机关事业单位养老保险；同时废止了 1978 年关于干部退休年龄的规定。城乡居民养老保险不受影响。 “小步调整、弹性实施”： 原定 2025 年前后退休的人只推迟几个月，越往后推迟越多。例如，1976 年出生的男性要到 2039 年才能领取养老金，而按原规定是 2036 年。1970 年代中期以后出生的一线女工推迟整整 5 年，代价最重。第三条允许职工与单位协商提前或推迟退休，但不得早于原法定年龄，并规定不得“违法强制或者变相强制”提前退休。 代价落在谁身上： 作者指出，1940 至 1960 年代出生、经历过国企下岗潮的一代人，养老金已明显提高；成本被转嫁给 1970 年代中期至 2000 年代初出生的人。这代人只经历过高度竞争的市场经济，也正经历电商平台带来的就业非正规化。 更隐蔽却更关键的条款： 第二条把领取养老金的最低缴费年限从 15 年提高到 20 年，2030 年 1 月才开始，每年提高半年，到 2040 年才完全生效。 背后的逻辑： 作者说，养老金的缴费率、替代率（退休金与退休前工资之比）、计算公式等技术细节容易“藏”起来，但几乎每个人都清楚自己几岁能领养老金。所以政府只能把代价推给注意力还在当下工资上的中青年。 三、为什么选择人大立法 此前的养老改革一直以国务院规章推动，这次却由人大立法，而且细节罕见地具体。 宪法依据： 人大宪法和法律委员会在表决前三天修改草案，加入“根据宪法”字样，援引宪法第四十四条关于退休制度的规定。 配套办法： 同时通过的《国务院关于渐进式延迟法定退休年龄的办法》附有四张详细的对照表。 程序： 人大会议议程公布时并未提及此事；草案在会议开幕前两天才提交，没有公开征求意见。作者指出，近年包括 2020 年香港国安法在内的立法，也都省去了公开征求意见这一环节。 作者的推测： 通常的做法是人大只定原则、由部委制定细则。这次直接写入细节，大概是为了防止部门之间讨价还价。 四、先拆“双轨制”：为改革铺路 起点： 2013 年十八届三中全会决定共 60 条，第 45 条列出多项养老改革目标，“研究制定渐进式延迟退休年龄政策”排在最后。 民意： 2013 年秋，《人民日报》在 11 个城市调查了 1,062 人，68.6% 选择“不支持，中国国情不适合”，外企员工中反对的比例高达 78.8%。72.9% 认为城职保与机关事业单位养老金之间的差距不合理，59% 赞成取消后者的非缴费制。这篇报道已从网上消失。2016 年《中国青年报》调查了 16.9 万人，91.1% 反对延迟退休。 “双轨制”改革： “双轨制”指企业职工自己缴费，而机关事业单位人员的养老金由财政全额负担。2009 年在五个省市试点，效果不一，广东还出现了提前退休潮。国务院 2014 年底出台决定，2015 年起把近 4,000 万机关事业单位人员纳入缴费制。经济专栏作家文贤堂 2013 年写道，改革双轨制“比延迟退休更重要、更紧迫”。 实际效果有限： 这项改革同样用过渡期“争取时间”，并配有补贴和职业年金。分析人士指出，改革后官员养老金仍约为城职保的两倍；改革前夕，国务院还给公务员加了薪。郑秉文认为，改革的动力来自对特权养老体制不满的非财政因素。作者还注意到：当时反腐运动正在推进，2013 至 2017 年据报约 169 万党员干部受到处分；但对官员养老待遇，中共仍给了充分的补偿。 五、十年反复放风与信誉成本 两部之争： 外界无从得知内部决策过程。作者推测，财政部担心城职保开支，人社部则顾虑就业。 谁在公开呼吁： 2012 至 2024 年间，公开有力呼吁延迟退休的领导人物都已退休，包括前财政部长楼继伟、前央行行长周小川，以及清华大学荣誉教授杨燕绥。 人社部长尹蔚民年年表态，迟迟没有方案： 2011 年称此事“非常复杂”。2014 年称 2020 年前一定推出方案。2016 年改口说方案须经中央批准后才能公布。2016 年夏提出“小步慢走、逐步到位、区分对待、分步实施”，官员称经五年过渡期后于 2022 年正式实施，但最终没有兑现。 搁置的原因： 中国人事科学研究院的庞诗 2021 年解释说，当时“时机不够成熟”，担心冲击就业市场。作者推测，2017 年十九大召开在即，也让领导层避免触碰这个话题。2012 年和 2017 年的党代会报告都没有提延迟退休，直到 2022 年二十大报告才写入。 转折点： 2020 年十九届五中全会写入“实施渐进式延迟法定退休年龄”。共产党员网的辅导材料称要“以减少社会震动，争取更多支持”。2021 年 2 月，习近平在政治局集体学习时说，一些国家推行延迟退休“实施得并不顺利”，要“把握好改革的方向、节奏和力度”。这篇讲话 2022 年 4 月才全文刊于《求是》。（编译）2021 年十四五规划确定“小步调整、弹性实施、分类推进、统筹兼顾”。2024 年 7 月三中全会提出“自愿、弹性”原则；两个月后，决定被“悄悄”列入人大常委会议程并获通过。 信誉成本： 作者认为，十多年来几乎年年放风，如果再不行动，中共可能面临信誉问题。 六、结论：事前的威权回应性与养老紧缩的走向 作者指出，这项改革恰好在习近平打破十年任期惯例两年之后落地。中共的做法包括：分阶段推迟、把成本转给年轻人、用详细立法固定改革、先推出受欢迎的双轨制改革、长期放风。这些手法在民主国家也不陌生。 作者借用学者 Christopher Heurlin 提出的“威权回应性”（authoritarian responsiveness），即政府监测民众反对，在反对蔓延时有选择地调整政策。他认为，延迟退休体现的是“事前”而非“事后”的回应：中央是这项政策唯一的制定者，无法把责任推给地方官员，只能小心铺垫。 展望未来，作者认为中共将继续用法律手段增加养老收入，同时控制支出： 增收： 2025 年 8 月，最高人民法院的解释认定企业与职工约定不缴社保的合同无效，9 月 1 日起施行。作者称社保缴费相当于工资的 24% 左右。这项规定施行后，企业和职工在社交媒体上纷纷抱怨负担加重。 控制支出： 2024 年，城乡居民养老保险覆盖 1.804 亿老人，月均仅 246 元。官方宣传已连续八年上调，起点是每月 55 元，十五五规划（2026–2030）也提出继续提高，但与城职保相比仍微不足道。 代价： 作者认为，这种做法牺牲了“共同富裕”和缩小城乡差距的承诺。在缺乏更有力的安全网时，养老紧缩还可能加剧预防性储蓄，阻碍经济转向消费驱动。

title: 宏福大火一年，消失的窗景

content: （宏福苑大火一年，端傳媒將陸續刊出 系列報導 ，敬請讀者留意。） 當窗外風景不再是廣福公園，朱太太把手作珠仔膠花放在新家的窗台。她的兒子想，她或許在重現亡夫種滿花草的窗台，但那朝夕淋花的老伴，卻不會回來了。一年前，朱先生的爸爸在宏昌閣家中，因大火離世。 每個家都有一扇窗。窗外是世界，窗內是家。看著窗，我們想出去；回家路上看到窗，卻急不及待想回去。 宏福苑的「宏」字，本指屋深響也。在倘大的家中，聚滿福氣，是對家的期許。但現在，窗外窗內再沒分野。心內心外，皆是飄泊。 這是宏福苑居民曾共同擁有，但最終失去的海景。圖：受訪者提供 9月起始，我們找尋宏福苑居民，希望走入他們的現居地拍攝窗口。我們前前後後聯絡過40位居民，有人一口答應，有人拒絕，也有人未再回覆。他們有的因為大火一周年將至，心情很壞，無法受訪。有居民一家暫住在親友物業，不想為親友帶來麻煩。有的則寄居於家人公屋，選擇低調過活。 最後留影的14個窗口散在香港各處。東至西貢清水灣，南至香港仔漁映樓，西至洪水橋樂翹樓，北至大埔三門仔善樓。一些居民的現居地臨近海水。藉著流動的海潮，是否可以就此洄游大埔吐露港？ 在早期的香港發展史裡，海景並不是富人獨享的景觀，宏福苑毗鄰吐露港，尋常人家也能在海邊組織家庭，建立生活。40年來，1984戶居民看著樹、看著海，這是他們共同的記憶。接受了原址無法重建，不能再共住大埔的事實，居民開始互相查問大家未來安置的去向，建立起小小的新群組。也許人即使被重創、被分散，仍會嘗試拉近彼此，重建群體的生活。 一場大火，把一個共同的風景，迸裂成不同的窗口、各異的現實。自此，宏福苑居民的人生將會通往何處？ 宏仁閣居民劉太於大火失去兩隻愛貓。她最後僅找回一個貓水兜，放在大埔過渡性房屋善樓的當眼處。攝：林振東/端傳媒 Phyllis 婚後由宏昌閣搬到西貢。大火後，她接了哥哥到現在的家居住，她在這裡學習蒸魚給哥哥吃。攝：林振東/端傳媒 朱爸爸在宏昌閣的主人房中罹難後，子女在大埔市中心為媽媽租了一個單位。在新居裡，朱媽媽和她的日常品都變得形單隻影。攝：林振東/端傳媒 宏泰閣居民 Tina 在一年間經歷大火與兒子移民，如今她住在兒子的物業，每天為對方開動心愛的古董馬場玩具。攝：林振東/端傳媒 宏昌閣居民 James 從元朗搬到香港仔漁映樓。這一年碰上大火，又要治療肝癌，他在這小小的過渡性房屋裡養病。攝：林振東/端傳媒 謝先生是宏仁閣居民，大火後最初一段時間，他身上只穿一件工作服，寄宿在教會的地方。攝：林振東/端傳媒 阿雯一家原本住在亡父名下物業宏志閣。他們起初期望能原址重建，如今只能物色一個可讓媽媽安享晚年的穩定居所。攝：林振東/端傳媒 宏建閣居民蔡先生年初由酒店搬到家人的新峰花園物業。他每月也會相約宏福苑街坊在大埔飲茶，又不時赴善樓探望街坊。攝：林振東/端傳媒 大火倖存者梁浩軒遷到烏溪沙的過渡性房屋，這一年他曾赴聽證會作供，講述逃生經歷。攝：林振東/端傳媒 宏新閣黃先生與家人這一年在策誠軒暫住。他將大火中去世的愛狗 Dor dor 的遺照放在電視旁邊，每天為牠點蠟燭。攝：林振東/端傳媒 鄧先生一家以前住在宏昌閣。他的小孩剛上初中，政府安排的安置房屋未能配合上學，他們唯有在大埔找地方落腳。攝：林振東/端傳媒 Dorz 和88歲的嫲嫲分別住在九龍啟福居上下層的單人單位，有事便 WhatsApp 溝通。這裡無法晾衣服，在廚房轉身便是床尾。攝：林振東/端傳媒 在大埔過渡性房屋策誠軒居住，宏泰閣居民歐太總有一種還沒回到家的感覺。攝：林振東/端傳媒 有些故事，不應被忽略 免費註冊端傳媒，與我們一起探索世界，理解時代。 立即註冊
